title: Our Lady of the Rosary: Lepanto, Pompeii, and the School of Prayer
summary: The title Our Lady of the Rosary brings together two related but historically distinct traditions: the Church's thanksgiving for the Christian victory at Lepanto on October 7, 1571, and the nineteenth-century revival of Rosary devotion at Pompeii through Blessed Bartolo Longo.

blocks.text: 1. A Necessary Historical Distinction

Our Lady of the Rosary at Pompeii and the historical devotion connected with Lepanto are distinct traditions rather than a single apparition event. Lepanto was a 1571 naval battle, while Pompeii is a 19th-century shrine and Rosary movement established by Blessed Bartolo Longo.
2. Lepanto and the Origin of the Feast

On October 7, 1571, the Holy League victory at the Battle of Lepanto was attributed to Mary's intercession following Pope St. Pius V's call for universal Rosary prayer. This led to the feast of Our Lady of Victory, later renamed Our Lady of the Rosary.

For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the cosmic powers over this present darkness, against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly places.
Exegesis: Christian struggle is fundamentally spiritual rather than earthly; the Rosary's true victories are won over sin, hatred, and spiritual darkness.
3. Pompeii and Blessed Bartolo Longo
In 1875, Bartolo Longo brought an image of Our Lady of the Rosary to Pompeii, revitalizing the spiritual and social life of the impoverished region through prayer, education, and charitable works.

blocks.title: The Interior Call of Blessed Bartolo Longo
blocks.text: “If you seek salvation, promulgate the Rosary. This is Mary's promise: anyone who propagates the Rosary will be saved.”
Longo also composed the famous Supplication to Our Lady of Pompeii, anchoring the sanctuary as an international center of Marian devotion and charity.
4. The Message of the Rosary
The Rosary serves as a school of the Gospel, meditating on the life of Christ through Mary's eyes to foster conversion, peace, and family prayer.

blocks.title: The Spiritual Center
blocks.text: Our Lady of the Rosary points to a Christ-centered prayer designed to contemplate Jesus with Mary, leading to interior conversion and active works of mercy.
5. Public and Private Revelation

The Rosary and its historical devotions draw their content from Gospel truths belonging to Public Revelation. Pious traditions connected to historical events like Lepanto remain devotional interpretations of divine providence.

blocks.title: CCC 67 and Pompeii
blocks.text: Pompeii is a approved shrine apostolate rather than a vision-based apparition. Its practices support Christian faith without imposing new dogmatic obligations.
6. Church Approval and Historical Status

The feast of Our Lady of the Rosary (October 7) and the Sanctuary of Pompeii hold full ecclesial approval. Pope John Paul II beatified Bartolo Longo in 1980, recognizing his witness as an apostle of the Rosary.

blocks.title: Approval and Status
blocks.text: The Rosary and the Pompeii shrine enjoy extensive liturgical and papal backing, validating the spiritual fruitfulness of the devotion rather than declaring a vision dogma.
But Mary treasured up all these things, pondering them in her heart.
Exegesis: Mary's contemplative posture serves as the model for the Rosary, inviting believers to ponder the mysteries of Christ repeatedly in their hearts.
7. Pastoral Application
Praying the Rosary should complement sacramental participation and inspire tangible acts of justice, peace, and service to the needy.

blocks.title: Central Lesson
blocks.text: Our Lady of the Rosary calls believers to contemplate Christ with Mary, transforming personal prayer into active peace, charity, and trust in divine providence.

blocks.title: Closing Prayer
blocks.text: O God of peace, you gave us the Rosary as a prayer in which the Church contemplates the mysteries of your Son with the Virgin Mary. Through the intercession of Our Lady of the Rosary, protect your people, convert our hearts, and bring peace to nations. Teach us to pray with faith and serve the poor as Blessed Bartolo Longo did. Our Lady of the Rosary, pray for us. Amen.
